name: History-lesson ad ("2,000 years ago people did X. Then the industry changed it for profit. Here's the version that goes back to the original")
cost_per_asset: $50-400 (AI period stills + image-to-video + VO) or $0 with archive art
length: 60-90s, 1080x1920 (and 4:5), documentary VO, era date stamps, big serif captions

shots.visual: AI period still animated in Kling: a Roman woman stepping into steaming baths, a gold bracelet catching light. Serif text: "Why Roman women never took their gold off". Era stamp "27 BC"
shots.audio_text: VO: "Two thousand years ago, Roman women wore their gold into the baths. Every single day."

shots.visual: Museum-style close-ups or AI renders: Egyptian collar, Byzantine ring, 1700s locket, all still shining
shots.audio_text: VO: "Real gold doesn't rust or tarnish. That's why these pieces still shine in museums."

shots.visual: AI 1950s factory line dipping brass in colour; cut to a modern $5 earring counter. Stamp "1952"
shots.audio_text: VO: "Then jewelry got cheap: brass with a coat of colour thinner than a hair."

shots.visual: Green-finger close-up, a tarnished chain in a drawer, rings taken off before a shower. Stamp "today"
shots.audio_text: VO: "By week three it's green and dull. We were taught that's normal. It isn't."

shots.visual: Qirra's hands at the workbench, PVD chamber B-roll, a necklace going into the ocean
shots.audio_text: VO: "Louise Carter went back to the original rule: jewelry you never take off. 14K gold bonded with PVD."

shots.visual: Stack on a wet wrist in the sea → product grid → "any 7 for $85"
shots.audio_text: VO: "Wear it like the Romans did." CTA: Shop the stack

prompts.prompt: Write a 75 s history-lesson ad for Louise Carter: hook set in the past with a date; 2-3 real, checkable facts about historical gold jewelry (list a source for each); how plated costume jewelry changed the category (no named competitor); today's visible letdown (green fingers, taking rings off to shower); LC as the return to the original (PVD 14K, waterproof); offer any 7 for $85. 150-200 words.

"Cinematic photoreal scene, ancient Roman bathhouse, steam, warm torchlight, a woman in a linen stola lowering herself into the water, a thick gold bracelet on her wrist catching the light, 35mm film grain, documentary lighting, 9:16"; one prompt per script line, same colour grade.
Slow push-in, 5 s per still, subtle steam/water movement, no face morphing; keep the jewelry shape fixed.
Calm documentary narrator, 150 wpm, low strings or room-tone ASMR under it.

qa_checklist: Hook lands in the first 1.5 s (video) or is readable at thumbnail size (static / slide 1).
Removal test: delete the product from the script. If it still makes sense, rewrite so the product is the payoff.
Matches the reference structure (same beat order and length band) before any creative twist.
Uses only real product imagery for the product; AI is for backgrounds, characters or b-roll, and is disclosed where required.
Every claim is on the brand's approved-claims list (PDP); no invented stats, reviews, doctors or customers.
Captions burned in and inside the safe zone; sound-off still understandable.
One clear CTA that matches the landing page offer.
Three hook variants delivered for the same body (test hooks, not whole new ads).
Avoid: Invented history kills trust: every fact needs a source in the doc before the edit.
Avoid: AI renders must not be presented as real museum artefacts; label AI where required.
Avoid: "Conspiracy" framing ("the industry is poisoning you") is a claim; keep the enemy to verifiable facts (plating wears off).
Avoid: Too long before the product: test 45 s and 90 s cuts; Voynov's examples run 75-117 s.
inputs: BRAND (name, product, price, offer, audience, proof points, banned claims)
ASSETS (real product photos/video, logo, fonts, colors)
outputs: brands/<brand-slug>.md with 3 concepts in the output schema below
